Initializer

skala_wrap_after_expression_lbrace #

A break in a wrapped initializer lands after the { rather than before it. Not read by the C# formatter. ⚠ Measured 2026-08-29 against the oracle at 2025.2.6 on constructs/wrapping/initializers.cs, one key at a time appended to the repository export in an [*.cs] section: at false — the only other value — the oracle returns the file byte-identical. Negative control in the same shape and on the same file: skala_wrap_array_initializer_style = chop_always rewrites it, so the file can move. A braced construct that wraps at all puts its braces on their own lines at either value; BreakPlan writes that unconditionally now. Skala honouring the key is what made this row SPURIOUS.

Typetrue / false
Defaulttrue
Default known fromthe Rider export, which is Rider's default for most keys and the author's choice for the rest, with nothing distinguishing the two
TierD — recorded so the key is not reported unknown; nothing reads it yet

skala_wrap_before_expression_rbrace #

A wrapped initializer’s } goes on a line of its own. Not read by the C# formatter. ⚠ The same measurement as skala_wrap_after_expression_lbrace, on the same file and in the same run: at false the oracle returns constructs/wrapping/initializers.cs byte-identical in both spellings, while skala_wrap_array_initializer_style = chop_always rewrites it. The } takes a line of its own at either value, which BreakPlan now writes unconditionally.
